label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
Hi Tolu, first of all, I'm sorry, I know that portal feeling. You asked for someone inside Biology 100L who wanted Medicine, so that's me. I'll tell you my own story and what I actually know, and you can decide from there.

Last year I wrote JAMB and got 251. I applied for Medicine and Surgery and they gave me Biology. I'm in a federal uni here in Lagos. The day I saw it on the portal, I locked myself in my cousin's room in Surulere and cried. I didn't even eat. And my mum had been telling people in church for like two months that I was doing medicine, so I had to beg her to stop. So whatever you're feeling right now, I get it, and it's not small.

Now the transfer gist, because that's what is confusing you. Kingsley is not correct that it's a myth, and favour is making it sound too simple. Transfer is real, but it is NOT easy, and nobody should accept Biology thinking it will happen automatically.

This is what our level adviser told us in my school. To move to MBBS after 100L you need a CGPA of at least 4.5 out of 5, AND there must be space. That second part is the one people forget. You can do everything right and still not get a place because there's no space. She told us that last year about 6 people were moved into Medicine from the whole faculty, and she thinks over 40 people applied. So you can see the numbers.

She also said you need to meet the Medicine cut-offs in both JAMB and post-UTME. I don't know your school's cut-offs or what you scored in post-UTME, so you have to check both. Your 268 is a very good score, but 268 alone doesn't establish that you're eligible. Please don't assume.

And I'll be honest about myself too, since you asked for honesty. My CGPA after first semester is 4.31. Not 4.5. I'm still trying, but I'm not sitting here telling you I've cracked it.

The 100L courses for us are BIO 101, CHM 101, PHY 101, MTH 101 and GST. Physics and maths are the ones dealing with people. If you're already strong in those, good for you, but if you're not, start preparing now, because that's where a 4.5 gets won or lost. Also some small money things nobody tells you: my lab coat was 6,500 naira, the dissecting kit was 9k, and the practical manual was extra. Nothing crazy, but budget for it.

You also asked if Biology itself is bad as a course or if it's only that your mind was on Medicine. For me it was mostly the second one. Biology is not a bad course at all. Our first BIO practical, we dissected toads. One guy in my group fainted, and I was fine. That was the day I realised I actually like this thing. I'm enjoying genetics and cell biology more than I expected, which I would never have believed on the day I was crying in Surulere.

On the rewrite side, I'm not going to tell you it's wrong, because it isn't, if you're ready for it. But I'll tell you something about someone I know so you can weigh it properly. My secondary school classmate Ifeoma rejected a Pharmacy offer so she could rewrite for Medicine. She has written JAMB two more times and she's still at home. I'm not saying that will be your story, 268 is a lot better than what many people have. I'm just saying a rewrite is also not guaranteed, and staying home is not as easy as people say. Favour is right about that part. You watch your mates go to school, and it can weigh on you.

So here's what I'd do if I were you, in this order:

1. Go to the faculty or the department of the school you were given and ask for the exact transfer rules for your own school. Ask about the CGPA requirement, whether there's a cut-off for JAMB and post-UTME for Medicine, how many people moved last session, and how many applied. Please don't just trust forum people, and that includes me. My school's rules may not be your school's rules. You have until the acceptance fee deadline, so use these two weeks to get real answers.

2. Check your own numbers against what they tell you: your JAMB score, your post-UTME score, and the Medicine cut-offs.

3. Ask yourself honestly if you want Medicine, or if you just want to be "doctor" for your parents. It sounds harsh, but I had to ask myself the same thing. If it's Medicine you really want, to the point you're ready to fight for a 4.5 or to rewrite, then that's your answer. If part of it is that everyone around you already told people you're a doctor in the making, it's worth knowing that before you spend another year or more chasing it.

Your dad and your aunty are both saying something real, by the way. Your dad is right that accepting keeps you moving and gives you a chance at transfer. Your aunty is right that Biology can end up being where you finish. Both can happen. Neither of them is lying to you.

Lastly, you did not fail. 268 is a big score, and getting an admission is not a small thing. Whatever you choose, accept and fight for the transfer, accept and settle into Biology, or reject and rewrite, it is not the end of the world. People find their way from every one of those roads. Give yourself a day or two to be sad, then go and ask the questions at the faculty.

You can message me here if you want to know anything about 100L. Wishing you well.

Amaka
